summary: Monthly sales counter feature validated end-to-end. New /api/merchants/top?limit=3 returns enriched discounts ordered by this-month redeemed counts; /api/discounts injects sales_this_month per discount; /api/auth/me now exposes has_active_subscription (true for subscribed clients, false otherwise, 401 for anon). E2E seeding of 4 redemptions in redemptions collection (redeemed status, current-month redeemed_at) correctly bumped a discount to #1 on /merchants/top and increased its sales_this_month. Old redemptions and pending redemptions are correctly ignored. Frontend smoke: DiscountCard renders data-testid=sales-counter-{id} ONLY for subscribed users (francesco: 4 badges rendered '+X venduti questo mese'); anonymous session shows 0 badges. /discounts page renders data-testid=top-shops-section with 1°/2°/3° badges. All 44 previous regression tests still green (1 skipped).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L664 `_month_start_iso()` compares stored redeemed_at strings via $gte — safe here because redeemed_at is always serialized with datetime.isoformat() including tzinfo (see L1286, L1300, L1321). Consider adding a doc-comment on the invariant so future code using naive datetimes doesn't break the counter.

enrich_discount now performs an extra db.redemptions.count_documents call per discount in the /discounts list (N+1). Fine for current seed size (<20 discounts) but should be replaced with a single $lookup or an aggregation once catalog grows (>100 discounts).
/api/merchants/top loops sequentially awaiting users + discounts inside the pipeline — could be batched with $lookup for lower latency, but current perf is acceptable.
server.py still 1997 lines with deprecated @app.on_event; already flagged in iter_13, non-blocking.
